solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, enumeration length); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing; the grid proves the blog's answer wrong at 17 down, corrected here

entries.clue: Church pour wine to honour God, but I won’t have it (8)

blocks.note: to libate is to pour out a drink offering to a god

annotation.surface: A churchgoer pours an offering of wine to God while someone else declines it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'I won't have it' reads like a refusal of the wine; it is the celibate speaking, declining sex.
annotation.definitionFit: A celibate person abstains from sex, so could say of it 'I won't have it'.

entries.clue: Copper on trial will be appealing in toto (6)

blocks.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

annotation.surface: A police officer facing a court case hopes to look sympathetic to the jury.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Copper' pushes toward a policeman on trial; it is the metal's symbol. 'In toto' turns 'appealing' into its superlative: appealing in total, the most appealing.
annotation.definitionFit: The cutest thing is the most appealing, appealing to the utmost degree.

entries.clue: Wealthy drunk (6)

blocks.note: slang: having had plenty to drink

annotation.surface: A rich person who has had too much to drink.
annotation.walkthrough: Both senses are slang, so neither half looks like the one to define with.
annotation.definitionFit: Loaded means both having plenty of money and having had plenty to drink.

entries.clue: Club game (9)

blocks.note: a club as a weapon: a short weighted cosh
the card game also called twenty-one or pontoon

annotation.surface: A sports club's fixture, or a nightclub's gaming table.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Club' looks like a golf club or a card suit; it is the cosh.
annotation.definitionFit: Blackjack names both a leather cosh and the casino card game.

entries.clue: I am torn and split after wrestling bouncer (12)

indicatorNotes.after wrestling: wrestled letters are thrown about and end up in a new shape

annotation.surface: A nightclub doorman complains that grappling with someone has left him torn and split.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bouncer' is set up as the doorman who wrestles; it is someone who bounces on a trampoline.
annotation.definitionFit: A trampolinist bounces for sport, so is literally a bouncer.

entries.clue: British artist stumped by Borders drug bust (6)

indicatorNotes.Borders: the artist borders the drug, lying on both sides of it

blocks.note: st = stumped, the cricket scorecard abbreviation

annotation.surface: A British artist is baffled by a drugs raid in the Scottish Borders.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Borders' looks like the Scottish region and 'bust' like a police raid; one is the container, the other a synonym for chest.
annotation.definitionFit: A bust is the chest, and breast is another word for it.

entries.clue: Folk group heading for successful careers (5)

indicatorNotes.heading for: the head of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: a race is a group of people

annotation.surface: A folk band is on its way to successful careers.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Careers' reads as a plural noun about jobs; it is the verb, to rush headlong.
annotation.definitionFit: To career is to rush along at speed, and so is to race.

entries.clue: For some Londoners, Yorkshire town’s sounding appropriate (8)

indicatorNotes.For some Londoners: Cockney Londoners famously drop the H at the start of a word, so the town loses its first letter
indicatorNotes.sounding: the name is taken as a Cockney pronounces it, not as it is spelt

blocks.note: a spa town in North Yorkshire

annotation.surface: A remark on how Londoners pronounce a Yorkshire town's name.
annotation.walkthrough: Cockneys, working-class East Londoners, famously drop the H, so HARROGATE becomes 'ARROGATE. 'Appropriate' is the verb, to seize.
annotation.definitionFit: To arrogate is to claim or appropriate something without right.

entries.clue: On becoming a part of it, fantastic as true love (8)

indicatorNotes.becoming a part of it: RE joins the letters to be rearranged

annotation.surface: Someone gushes that true love is fantastic once you are part of it.
annotation.walkthrough: RE joins AS TRUE before the rearrangement, making a composite anagram. 'Love' is the term of endearment.
annotation.definitionFit: Treasure and love are both fond names for a dear person.

entries.clue: Rip off an unruly person (8)

blocks.note: the verb: to pull something off by force, read as two words

annotation.surface: A swindle pulled by a troublemaker.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rip off' looks like the noun, a con; it is the verb phrase, to tear away.
annotation.definitionFit: A tearaway is a wild, unruly youngster; tear away is to rip something off.

entries.clue: Come into possession of a company in hearing (6)

indicatorNotes.in hearing: what is heard, not what is written

blocks.note: a crew is a company of people

annotation.surface: A company acquires something in a court hearing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In hearing' looks like a court session; it signals the sound. 'Company' is a band of people, not a business.
annotation.definitionFit: To accrue is to gain or accumulate, to come into possession of something over time.

entries.clue: Unctuous, base criminal gets under one’s skin (12)

indicatorNotes.criminal: the letters are crooked, out of their lawful order

annotation.surface: An oily, low-down crook really gets on your nerves.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Gets under one's skin' reads as the idiom for irritating; here 'gets' is a link and 'under one's skin' is literal.
annotation.definitionFit: A literal gloss of the Latin: sub (under) and cutis (skin), the medical term for tissue or injections beneath the skin.

entries.clue: State summit Soviet leader fronts (5)

indicatorNotes.leader fronts: the first letter goes in front

annotation.surface: A Soviet leader heads a state summit.
annotation.walkthrough: 'State' and 'summit' read together as a diplomatic meeting; 'State' is the verb, to say.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, verb for verb: to say something aloud in words.

entries.clue: Additional indicators of drunken nips and slugs (4,5)

indicatorNotes.drunken: the letters stagger out of order

annotation.surface: Telltale signs of someone having knocked back yet more nips and slugs of spirits.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Additional indicators' look like extra clues to drinking; they are the symbols of addition.
annotation.definitionFit: Plus signs are the symbols that indicate addition.

entries.clue: One might be on a trip in Hull with raincoat on (12)

annotation.definition: One might be on a trip

indicatorNotes.on: a raincoat put on is worn differently; the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: A tourist on a trip to rainy Hull, a port in northern England, wears a raincoat.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Trip' reads as a journey to Hull; it is a drug trip.
annotation.definitionFit: A hallucinator sees things that are not there, as someone on an LSD trip does.

entries.clue: Thriller in which cop perhaps holsters piece (9)

indicatorNotes.holsters: a holster holds a gun, as NAILER holds BIT

blocks.note: one who nails, catches, a criminal

annotation.surface: A crime thriller in which a policeman carries a gun in his holster.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Piece' looks like a gun going into the holster; it is a bit.
annotation.definitionFit: A nailbiter is a tense thriller that keeps you biting your nails.

entries.clue: Killed without reason? (8)

blocks.note: an end is a purpose or reason

annotation.surface: A question about a senseless killing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Without' means outside here, not lacking. The whole clue doubles as the definition: to kill without reason is to have offended.
annotation.definitionFit: Anyone who has killed for no reason has committed an offence, so has offended.

entries.clue: Predatory flapper cut by husband with one sword (8)

indicatorNotes.cut by: the bird is cut open and H and I go into the gap

blocks.note: a falcon is a bird of prey

annotation.surface: A menacing 1920s flapper girl, slashed by her husband wielding a sword.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Flapper' suggests a 1920s girl; it is something with flapping wings. Husband and one sit together as a pair inside the bird.
annotation.definitionFit: A falchion is a broad curved medieval sword.

entries.clue: Honest mug acquiring side-swiped Benz for Swiss Baron (12)

indicatorNotes.side-swiped: Benz loses its sides, B and Z

blocks.note: BENZ with its sides swiped off
a stein is a beer mug

annotation.surface: A straight-talking fool is given a battered Mercedes in exchange for a Swiss aristocrat.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mug' looks like a fool; it is a beer mug. Victor Frankenstein in Mary Shelley's novel is from Geneva; the films made him a Baron.
annotation.definitionFit: Baron Frankenstein, the Genevan scientist who builds the monster, is the Swiss baron.

entries.clue: I take orders from soldier behind blockade (6)

indicatorNotes.behind: the soldier comes after the blockade

blocks.note: a man is a private soldier

annotation.surface: A soldier on a barricade says he takes his orders from a superior.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Orders' look military, from a soldier; they are drinks orders taken across a bar.
annotation.definitionFit: A barman takes customers' drinks orders.

entries.clue: One of The Animals with a sound like Lennon? (6)

indicatorNotes.with a sound like: the answer is a word that sounds the same as what Lennon was

annotation.surface: A member of the 1960s band The Animals who sounds like John Lennon.
annotation.walkthrough: The Animals were a 1960s band, so the capital T looks like a band name; read as plain animals, a beetle is one of them.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: an insect counts among the animals once the band's capitals are ignored.

entries.clue: After messing up, men I scorn turn red (9)

indicatorNotes.After messing up: the letters are messed up into a new order

annotation.surface: Men blush with shame after being scorned for a blunder.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Turn red' looks like blushing; it is the verb, to make crimson.
annotation.definitionFit: A rare, literary verb built from crimson, a deep red, with the en- prefix meaning to make.

entries.clue: Old people notice nice-looking houses (5)

indicatorNotes.houses: the phrase houses the answer inside it

annotation.surface: Elderly people spot attractive homes.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Houses' looks like the noun, homes; it is the verb, to contain. The Iceni were the ancient British tribe led by Boudicca.
annotation.definitionFit: A tribe of Iron Age East Anglia, so a people of long ago: 'people' in the sense of a nation.

entries.clue: Black pilot circles river to give chopper support (5)

indicatorNotes.circles: to circle something is to go all the way round it, so the pilot's letters surround the river's

blocks.note: an ace is a top fighter pilot

annotation.surface: A pilot in a black helicopter circles a river to support the aircraft.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Chopper' looks like the helicopter the pilot flies; choppers are teeth, which a dental brace supports.
annotation.definitionFit: A brace is a dental device that supports and straightens teeth, slangily choppers.

entries.clue: Swinger’s club in Germany associated with Amazon? (6)

indicatorNotes.associated with: things associated with each other go together, so Germany's letter joins the river's name

blocks.note: D is Germany's international vehicle code
the Amazon is a river, a definition by example

annotation.surface: A German swingers' club linked with the online giant Amazon.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Swinger's club' suggests a sex club; the swinger is a golfer and the club a driver. 'Amazon' is the river, not the company.
annotation.definitionFit: A driver is the golf club a golfer swings for long shots.

entries.clue: Tory MP involved in offensive disregard of authority (8)

indicatorNotes.involved in: to be involved in something is to be caught up inside it, so MP sits within the offensive

blocks.note: the Tet offensive of the Vietnam War, 1968

annotation.surface: A Conservative member of parliament is caught up in a rude show of defiance.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Offensive' reads as the adjective, rude; it is the noun, the Tet offensive. A Tory is a British Conservative.
annotation.definitionFit: The legal sense, as in contempt of court: wilful defiance of a court or other authority.

entries.clue: Exhausted fellow, one from Germany (4,2)

blocks.note: a don is a university fellow

annotation.surface: A tired colleague, a single visitor from Germany.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fellow' is a university fellow, which in Oxford and Cambridge is a don.
annotation.definitionFit: An informal British idiom for worn out, as after a long day's work.

entries.clue: Contract row in NHS unit (8)

indicatorNotes.in: the row is placed in the unit, its letters inside the hospital department's

blocks.note: A&E = accident and emergency, a hospital department
a string is a row or series

annotation.surface: A dispute over a staff contract in a National Health Service department.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Contract' and 'row' suggest an employment dispute; 'row' rhymes with 'go' here, a line of things. The NHS is Britain's state health service, and A&E is its emergency department.
annotation.definitionFit: To astringe is to contract or draw together, as astringents do to tissue.
